title: IdP attribute handshake, RBAC v2 mapping, and SSO compatibility playbook (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping)
creator: Nina Kapoor
description: Deliver a focused compatibility playbook and implementation guidance for SAML IdP integrations (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping) that maps incoming assertions into RBAC v2 principals, defines audit logging schema for mapping decisions, and specifies admin controls and UI behavior. This ticket covers: (1) canonical attribute parsing rules and fallback heuristics, (2) deterministic role/group mapping rules for RBAC v2 including precedence and resolution when multiple attributes conflict, (3) audit log fields to capture mapping inputs and outcomes, (4) required console admin controls (mapping preview, dry-run mode, import/export mapping rules), (5) automated test harnesses and acceptance test cases per IdP, and (6) known IdP quirks and recommended mitigation patterns. Deliverables: a Confluence playbook, a JSON schema for audit events, sample SAML assertions per IdP, integration tests in the sso-test-harness repo, and a small feature PR to the Console that exposes a mapping dry-run endpoint and preview UI component.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with per-IdP sections and troubleshooting checklist
Audit event JSON schema reviewed and approved by Security; events include assertion_id, idp_provider, saml_nameid, received_attributes, mapped_principals, mapping_version, decision, and reason
Automated tests validate mapping behavior for at least Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping using the sso-test-harness
Console mapping preview supports dry-run for both single-user assertions and group-import snapshots
Backward-compatible defaults preserved: existing customers with current mapping rules see no behavioral changes after rollout unless they opt into v2 mappings

idp_quirks_and_mitigation: Okta: groups sometimes present as 'groups' attribute or as 'memberOf' depending on app integration. Mitigation: check both, normalizer prefers 'groups' then 'memberOf'. Provide admin mapping rule examples for both.

Azure AD: custom claim pipelines may return JSON-encoded arrays in a single attribute value. Mitigation: detect JSON array string and parse safely with size limit and fallback to single-token parsing.
Google Workspace: NameID can be email or persistent id depending on SAML app; don't assume 'email' is present—fall back to subject/NameID, then to email attribute if provided.

Ping: assertion timestamps sometimes have millisecond precision and nonstandard timezone string; normalize via server-side parser and accept up to 5s clock skew by default. Admin can tighten skew in tenant settings.
mapping_rules_examples: Example A (preferred): attribute 'roles' -> split on comma -> lookup role in RBAC v2 mapping table -> assign principals in order of specificity (role mapping > group mapping > default-role)
Example B (group-first): attribute 'groups' -> map each group to a principal; if multiple principals conflict, apply 'highest privilege wins' unless tenant sets 'explicit deny' rules
Example C (SCIM fallback): if assertion lacks authoritative group info, fall back to SCIM delta snapshot if provisioning enabled; dry-run separately logs which path was used
risks: Mis-mapping high-privilege roles when multiple attributes present; mitigated by explicit admin preview and dry-run
Excessive audit volume if we log full attribute payloads for large groups; mitigated by summarization (capture hashes and sample items) and a tenant-level audit-sampling config
IdP inconsistencies causing flaky e2e tests; mitigated by running harness against recorded assertions in CI and a small number of live smoke tests per IdP
implementation_notes: Server-side: add AttributeNormalizer module with pluggable parsers per IdP and a canonical output: list of {name, values}
Mapping engine: deterministic policy evaluation order (explicit deny -> role mappings -> group mappings -> default). Record mapping_version on every decision.
Audit: store full raw assertion in encrypted blob only when tenant opts in; otherwise store sampled attributes plus a md5 hash of full assertion for traceability.
Console: mapping preview uses dry-run API; show a compact diff and a confidence score when heuristics were applied
